composition.value: Commons’ blanket expiry metadata is unreliable: it gives the wrong composer death year.
composition.note: Stravinsky died in 1971, not 1936. The 1910 score is described as public domain in the United States by the score catalogue, but not generally in life-plus-70 jurisdictions. The US government-work status of a band transcription or recording does not remove rights in the underlying composition.

alternatives.value: Stravinsky died in 1971; the 1910 score has territory-dependent copyright status, not blanket life-plus-70 expiry.

recording.value: PD-USGov-Military-Marine: transcription, performance and recording described as works of US Marine personnel.
recording.note: The file page attributes Thomas Knox’s transcription, the band’s performance and the Marine recording to official US government work. This is a US public-domain basis for those contributions, not worldwide clearance of Stravinsky’s underlying composition.

rights.creditLine: Igor Stravinsky, Infernal Dance from The Firebird; transcribed by Thomas Knox; “The President’s Own” United States Marine Band, Colonel John R. Bourgeois as credited. US Marine government-work recording, via Wikimedia Commons. Underlying composition rights are territory-dependent; Commons’ composer death year is erroneous.
